criteria.text: `public/compare.html` exists, is valid, self-contained HTML/CSS/JS (no build step, no external JS dependency beyond Google Fonts), and loads without console errors when served by `pnpm dev` and opened at `/compare.html`.
On load, both person `<select>` elements are populated from `GET /api/people` and default to two distinct people (manual check against the fixture/seeded data: e.g. Lula and Tarcísio).

Changing the shared `days`/`source`/`kind`/`min`/`sort`/`limit` controls issues exactly two `GET /api/people/:id/graph` requests (one per side) with identical query-string values for every parameter except `id`, verifiable via browser devtools network tab.

Given person A's and B's node lists, the three columns partition `idsA ∪ idsB` with no overlap and no omission: `|exclusiveA| + |shared| + |exclusiveB| = |idsA ∪ idsB|`, and `shared = idsA ∩ idsB` exactly, checkable by manually comparing a small fixture-backed pair of responses against the rendered columns.

Selecting the same person for A and B does not error, does not block the fetch, renders a "comparando a mesma pessoa" pt-BR notice, and results in `exclusiveA = exclusiveB = []` (manual check: both columns empty, shared column = full list).

Clicking a chip toggles a visible highlight state on that chip only; clicking it again removes the highlight; clicking a different chip moves the highlight (never two chips highlighted at once). Manual check.

With both filters set so no docs are `about` either person (e.g. `days=1` on the fixture's 100-day-old-only doc scenario, or `min` above any real count), all three columns show the "nada nessa janela." empty state, not a blank/broken layout.

If one side's fetch is made to fail (e.g. temporarily point one `id` at a nonexistent person id via URL manipulation, which 404s), that side's column area shows the pt-BR error copy instead of throwing a JS exception, and the other two columns still render correctly from the succeeding side (treating the failed side as `[]`).

`public/design-5.html` diff is limited to: (a) the new `.compare-link` anchor placed between `.person-pick` and `#stats` inside the existing `<header>`, and (b) its companion CSS rule(s) inside the existing `<style>` block. No other markup, script, or style in `design-5.html` changes — checkable via `git diff public/design-5.html` showing only additive header/CSS lines.
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` both still pass unmodified (this feature adds no `.ts` files and no server route, so neither suite's behavior changes) — checkable by running both commands.

Page is visually usable at exactly 1440×900 viewport: header, shared toolbar, and all three columns are visible without horizontal scroll and without columns collapsing/overlapping (manual visual check, the human review gate for this issue per the brief).
Node chips never display a coerced-to-zero tone value; `tone: null` nodes render with no tone indicator (manual code-read check: no `?? 0` or `|| 0` applied to `.tone` anywhere in `compare.html`).
